items.title: ورود نیروهای دولتی عراق به پایگاه کتائب حزب‌الله، از گروه‌های مورد حمایت ایران، در جرف‌نصر

items.summary_original: Former President Joe Biden’s new memoir has drawn sharp criticism and opened a debate about how Biden’s choices — and his account of them — will shape his legacy. Released Nov. 17, "Promise Me, America" defends Biden’s presidency and his decision to seek re-election in 2024. The memoir drew a sharp verdict from The New Yorker writer Amy Davidson Sorkin, who said Biden remains "stubbornly in denial," while other critics scrutinized the book's account of Gaza and what it left out about racial equity. Sorkin’s criticism centers on Biden’s response to questions about his age and his continued insistence that he could have won. "The true test of a book like this is whether its author will own his losses, too. Biden, for his part, does not," added New York Times nonfiction critic Jennifer Szalai. "He is so preoccupied with burnishing his legacy that he gets awkward and defensive when addressing the two issues many readers will be most curious about: his handling of the war in Gaza, and his decision to run for a second term." "The news of the memoir, in short, is that there is no real news: Biden is as stubbornly in denial as ever, " Sorkin wrote. items.summary: به گزارش نیویورک پست، جنیفر لاگنر پس از بازشماری های متوالی که باعث شد او با رقیبش برابری کند، با پرتاب سکه در انتخابات برای کمیسر شهر ساحل آتلانتیک در فلوریدا پیروز شد. لاگنر و لیزا هرولد هر کدام با 3162 رای پس از اینکه جری هالند، ناظر انتخابات شهرستان دووال، شروع به بازشماری دستی و ماشینی کرد، هر کدام با 3162 رای انتخاب شدند. این بن بست هفته گذشته باعث شد که یک تای شکن منحصر به فرد آغاز شود که در آن هر نامزد شانس برنده شدن دو تا از سه ورق سکه را خواهد داشت. سه تیم فوتبال دبیرستان سرنوشت پلی آف خود را با پرتاب سکه در پارکینگ نیمه شب تعیین می کنند. هرولد اول رفت و هدها را صدا زد، اما سکه در دم فرود آمد و لاگنر 1-0 پیش افتاد. لاگنر در مرحله بعدی قرار گرفت و به طور دقیق سرها را پیش بینی کرد
items.summary_original: Jennifer Lagner won the election for Atlantic Beach city commissioner in Florida via a coin toss after successive recounts left her tied with her opponent, according to the New York Post. Lagner and Lisa Herrold each sat at 3,162 votes after Duval County's Supervisor of Elections Jerry Holland initiated both a manual and a machine recount. The deadlock initiated the unique tiebreaker last week in which each candidate would have the chance to win two of three coin flips. THREE HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL TEAMS HAVE THEIR PLAYOFF FATES DECIDED BY A MIDNIGHT PARKING LOT COIN TOSS Under the city's election rules, each candidate had a chance to call the coin's landing. Herrold went first, calling heads, but the coin landed tails, giving Lagner a 1-0 lead. Lagner went next, accurately predicting heads to win the contest, securing her election victory to become city commissioner. "This shows how great and free our country is," Lagner told a local news outlet. "I am honored to have the opportunity to serve as your next City Commissioner for Seat 4," she wrote on Facebook. "A coin toss was certainly an unexpected and unforgettable way to bring an election to a close! Thank you to Jerry Holland and his entire team for their work throughout this election process." "Jen and I have been a part of this community for years ... It was meant to be ... We’re going to look back at this and realize how unbelievable this was," Herrold told the local outlet. items.summary_original: FIRST ON FOX: President Donald Trump and UFC President and CEO Dana White will announce six-figure personal contributions to one of America's oldest musical institutions. The President’s Own United States Marine Band played a key role in America's 250th birthday celebrations and official state business this year — and a White House official tells Fox News Digital that the pair want to "express their appreciation for the band’s exceptional talent, professionalism and commitment to excellence." Trump and White are scheduled to announce Friday afternoon that they will each donate $100,000 of their own money, which will give each member of the band approximately $1,000. No taxpayer dollars will be used for the $200,000 gift. The announcement will be made during the first-ever event on the new White House helipad on the South Lawn. All 135 members of the band will attend alongside senior military leaders, including Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao and Commandant of the Marine Corps General Eric Smith. items.summary_original: Following the GOP’s widespread midterm losses, Sen. Josh Hawley , R-Mo. — who in September indicated to the Washington Examiner that he had "no intention" of running for president in 2028 — is now leaving the door open to a White House bid. "After this most recent election, I think everybody that cares about the future of the party, the future of the country, has a lot of thinking to do," the senator said to The Associated Press when asked about his presidential aspirations. "So I’ll just say I have a lot of thinking to do." Democrats delivered a midterm election drubbing and will control the House and Senate majorities next year. JOSH HAWLEY SHOOTS DOWN PROSPECT OF 2028 WHITE HOUSE BID, SAYS HE HAS 'NO INTENTION' OF RUNNING: REPORT "I was alarmed by the results of the election, and I’m concerned about the direction of both my party and the country," Hawley told NBC News when asked whether he is thinking about running for president. "And I want to do my part there. I’m trying to think through what my part is. But I certainly want to do my part for the future." "Listen, I don’t want to give you a misconception that, for sure, I have plans or intentions," he noted, according to the outlet. "What I said to you is the honest to goodness truth, which is just that I’ve got four years here to serve in the Senate, and I’m just trying to think about where I am and what’s in front of me, what can I do to help the country go forward." "I'm concerned about what comes next for the party.

items.summary_original: Just hours after Russian President Vladimir Putin stood alongside President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at a historic summit in China, Moscow unleashed one of its largest attacks on Ukraine, killing at least eight people, striking three major bridges in Kyiv and sending suspected Russian missiles and a drone into NATO-member Poland. The massive overnight assault Friday came as the Trump administration announced progress toward expanding peace negotiations with Russia, exposing the stark contrast between the diplomatic optimism emerging from Thursday's meetings and the escalating war on the ground. A European intelligence source told Fox News Digital that Putin is preparing an intensified winter military campaign and believes that a combination of sustained battlefield pressure and U.S.-led diplomatic negotiations could eventually force Ukraine to surrender additional territory. items.summary_original: The Republican chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee has warned of an ongoing ‘horrific trend’ of Christians being killed in Africa . Earlier this month, at least 34 people, the majority said to be Ethiopian Orthodox Christians, were killed in a village in the Arsi Zone, about 250 miles southeast of Ethiopia’s capital, Addis Ababa. "The attacks on Christians in Ethiopia are a horrific trend," Sen. Jim Risch, R-Idaho, told Fox News Digital in a statement, adding, "The instability and violence in Ethiopia has grave consequences for Ethiopian civilians, the region and American interests." NIGERIAN PASTOR HIGHLIGHTED BY TRUMP SAYS HE’S NEXT AFTER MILITIA KILLS HIS RELATIVES Open Doors UK Ireland told Fox News Digital there has been a string of killings in the area, with some 60 Orthodox Christians killed just two weeks before this attack in November. Open Doors is an international organization supporting persecuted Christians. A State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital they are aware of "reports of killing in Arsi Zone," adding: "Reports of civilian killings in Ethiopia demand action. We call for independent investigations and accountability." The Addis Standard online news outlet reported gunmen approached St. Mary’s Church in Endeto, Robe District, and at the main entrance shouted "Surrender" before opening fire. items.summary: اولین روز پنج شنبه آنتروپیک در بازار سهام، به ارزش حدود 1.5 تریلیون دلار، بزرگترین در تاریخ آمریکا است و با توجه به وعده هایی که توسط بنیانگذاران آن داده شده است، احتمالاً مقدمه ای برای سیل تاریخی مشابهی از پول نقد به سیستم سیاسی است. بلومبرگ پیش‌بینی می‌کند که هر یک از هفت بنیانگذار Anthropic اکنون که شرکت هوش مصنوعی آن‌ها به صورت عمومی درآمده است، تقریباً 24.5 میلیارد دلار ارزش خواهد داشت. هر یک از این هفت نفر همچنین متعهد شده‌اند که 80 درصد از سهام خود را در شرکت به اهداف بشردوستانه اختصاص دهند - قولی که با توجه به پیوند آنتروپیک با فلسفه اخلاقی بحث‌برانگیز و تاریخچه هزینه‌های کلان آن برای تأثیرگذاری بر انتخابات، ابروها را برانگیخت. نوع دوستی مؤثر، که برخی از سرمایه‌گذاران و کارمندان اولیه آنتروپیک از آن حمایت کرده‌اند، عموماً با حجم وسیع سیاسی و فیزی برخورد می‌کند.
items.summary_original: Anthropic’s Thursday stock market debut, valued at around $1.5 trillion, is the largest in American history and, given promises made by its founders, is likely the preface to a similarly historic flood of cash into the political system. Bloomberg projects that each of Anthropic’s seven co-founders will be worth approximately $24.5 billion now that their artificial intelligence firm has gone public. Each of the seven has also pledged to give away 80% of their equity in the firm to philanthropic causes — a promise that has raised eyebrows given Anthropic’s links to a controversial moral philosophy and its history of spending big to influence elections. Effective altruism, which some of Anthropic’s early funders and employees have voiced support for, generally treats massive political and philanthropic giving as a moral obligation to prevent AI "doomsday" scenarios, such as a rogue agent working to exterminate the human race. Though the company's founders have distanced themselves from the movement, some early employees and other figures associated with Anthropic have maintained connections to its ideas, particularly its emphasis on preventing potentially catastrophic risks from artificial intelligence. Politically, this has manifested as Anthropic's leaders throwing large sums of money behind efforts to regulate AI development . items.summary_original: Elon Musk’s SpaceX has hired a team of veteran Washington lobbyists with Democratic connections as the party prepares to take control of Congress and intensify scrutiny of his business empire. Democratic lawmakers have signaled plans to investigate several aspects of Musk’s business dealings and government relationships, including allegations that SpaceX improperly restricted Ukraine’s satellite communications, whether the Pentagon has become overly dependent on the company and potential conflicts of interest stemming from Musk’s relationship with the Trump administration. Against that backdrop, newly released public records show SpaceX has retained five veteran lobbyists from Mehlman Consulting, a bipartisan D.C.-based government affairs firm, several of whom have deep ties to Democratic lawmakers and former administrations. SpaceX, with a market capitalization of nearly $2 trillion, is home to Musk's holdings in aerospace engineering, artificial intelligence, telecommunications and space transportation . If Democrats successfully knock it down a peg, the resulting loss in value could send shock waves throughout the economy. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump is set to face reporters Friday after wrapping up a historic visit to China that brought him together with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin for unprecedented three-way talks. The leaders struck a warm diplomatic tone despite lingering questions over the war in Ukraine, nuclear arms negotiations and tensions in the Middle East — as well as stalled trade negotiations between the U.S. and China. The summit in Shenzhen marked the first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia, bringing Trump face-to-face with two of America's chief geopolitical adversaries. Washington has spent years arming Ukraine in its war against Russia, while the Pentagon has long identified China as its primary "pacing challenge" in the Indo-Pacific. Trump's scheduled press conference at noon on Friday will offer an opportunity to elaborate on what the meetings accomplished and whether the diplomatic discussions will lead to concrete agreements. items.summary_original: A leading pro-life group said it opposed advancing Heidi Overton's nomination to lead the Food and Drug Administration without commitments from the Trump administration on abortion drug policy. The White House withdrew her nomination this week amid questions about her support in the Senate. In an interview with Fox News Digital, Erik Baptist, senior vice president of legal strategy at Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America, said his group asked the Senate to hold up Overton’s confirmation until it received "firm commitments" from the administration on two fronts regarding abortion drug policy. Baptist said the group wants the next FDA nominee to commit to ending mail-order access to abortion drugs authorized under the Biden administration and changing how the agency studies the safety of those pills. "Right now, we’re seeing more abortions in this country than before the Supreme Court’s decision overturning Roe v. Wade," Baptist said. "That’s precisely because of what the Biden FDA did to authorize mail-order abortion drugs. We’re seeing upwards of 15,000 abortion drugs and abortions occurring in pro-life states. items.summary_original: Senate Republicans scored a major win after advancing a massive bill that would overhaul America’s permitting system in a bid to turbocharge infrastructure and energy development in the country. The Senate advanced the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA) on a major bipartisan vote Thursday night. The legislation went through fits and starts over the last few months, until a bipartisan coalition, with buy-in from the White House, formed to tinker with the final product. At the 30,000-foot level, the sweeping package would accelerate environmental review of projects, limit legal challenges, protect approved projects, expand the electric grid and streamline energy development in all fields — like oil, gas and renewables. AMERICA’S BROKEN PERMITTING SYSTEM IS QUIETLY RAISING YOUR COST OF LIVING "This is a major step toward making it faster and more efficient and easier to build infrastructure projects, certainly without giving up any of the strong protections for our environment," Senate Environment and Public Works Committee Chair Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va., said when the bill was introduced in September. The bill also tackles an issue that was front and center for voters across the country: data centers . Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., the Democratic lead on the legislation, pushed for stronger language in the bill that would shield ratepayers from higher costs that stem from data center development and their usage of electricity. items.summary_original: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is out after President Donald Trump backed his firing over concerns he lacked the cybersecurity credentials for the job, Fox News has confirmed. Kirsten A. Davies, the Pentagon’s chief information officer, will step into the position in an acting capacity. Davies, who was Senate-confirmed, will join Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, White House technology advisor Michael Kratsios and Secretary of State Marco Rubio on the administration's national security and cyber leadership team. An administration official separately told Fox News that Cairncross did not want to serve another two years in the role. Cairncross took office Aug. 4, 2025, after Senate confirmation, and the exact date of his departure remains unclear. TIMELINE: AMERICA HITS A TECH WALL AS OUTAGES CRIPPLE EMAIL, GROUND FLIGHTS AND DISRUPT MAJOR BANKS Senior administration officials welcomed Davies' appointment on X. "Congratulations to the new National Cyber Director Kirsten Davies — look forward to working together to strengthen America’s cybersecurity," Rubio wrote. Clayton praised her background, writing, "With nearly two decades of leadership experience in the technology space, Kirsten Davies will be a strong asset for the Trump administration in her new position with the Office of the National Cyber Director. "I wouldn't take my family there right now," retired Sgt. Betsy Brantner Smith, a spokesperson for the National Police Association , told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview. Smith's warning follows Mamdani's announcement that the NYPD's Strategic Response Group (SRG), a roughly 500-officer specialized unit involved in counterterrorism, major event security and protest response, will be disbanded as part of a broader overhaul of how the nation's largest police department handles demonstrations. MAMDANI GUTS ELITE NYPD TACTICAL UNIT, BACKS 'CIVILIAN-LED APPROACH' TO RESPONDING TO PROTESTS The democratic socialist mayor has defended the decision as fulfilling a campaign promise to separate counterterrorism operations from the policing of constitutionally protected protests. Critics, however, argue that dismantling the established unit could undermine the coordination and specialized training needed to respond to emergencies. Smith, who spent 29 years in Chicago-area law enforcement and has experience supervising crowd control operations, said the consequences could extend beyond protests. It examined how legal commercial partnerships transferred advanced technology and manufacturing expertise to Chinese military-linked companies. China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) is the country's military, which the committee says has benefited from civilian aerospace technology transfers. "American and European companies transferred technology to China that could be used against our brave men and women in uniform. items.summary_original: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling on the U.S. to quickly organize talks with Russia with the full participation of European negotiators and advisors in what would mark a first-of-its-kind meeting. He made the call Thursday after meeting with several U.S. and European leaders in Berlin at the Coalition of the Willing summit, which focused on security guarantees aimed at deterring future Russian aggression. During the meeting, U.S. special envoy Jared Kushner announced that Moscow and President Donald Trump had agreed to a multilateral negotiating format involving Europe. "We are counting on the American side to help organize the first multilateral meeting at the team level, with full European participation, as soon as possible," Zelenskyy said. The push signals an effort to prevent Europe and Kyiv from being sidelined in U.S.-Russia talks . KUSHNER, WITKOFF SET FOR KYIV TALKS AFTER PUTIN MEETING IN US PUSH FOR PEACE "From the very beginning, Ukraine has advocated for this approach — maximum coordination among us on everything concerning European and Ukrainian security and our future," Zelenskyy said. "We need to work quickly, and this is the only approach Ukraine is taking. The more actively the discussions move forward, the greater the chances of achieving real progress." items.summary_original: Democrats are fretting that the "Bloc" of progressives will lug House Democrats to the left. But, there is strength in numbers. Yours truly wanted to understand just how much sway progressives might have over the House Democratic Caucus. Look no further than Wednesday morning’s vote for speaker. No one challenged House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) to become speaker-designate in the internal caucus vote. It’s about the math. Jeffries marshaled 251 of the 262 secret ballots cast. The recorded vote revealed that despite all of their noise and clamor, extreme progressives really don’t have much juice compared to the rest of the Democratic Caucus. In fact, rank-and-file Democrats crushed their progressive colleagues. Democrats did not vote by name. But numbers say a lot. While the recorded vote could have revealed potential craters of dissent among Democrats and questions about Jeffries, the tally registered the opposite. It showed just how diminutive the hard left is in the Democratic Caucus. JEFFRIES BRUSHES OFF OPPOSITION FROM FAR-LEFT DEMS WHO VOTED NO: 'WE’RE GOING TO WORK TOGETHER' Do they exude an outsized political voice? Yes. But success in Congress is measured in numbers. And at least on Wednesday, the numbers signaled few results for the Bloc and a show of unity among Democrats. items.summary_original: As Anthropic executives gathered inside the Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square on Thursday morning to ring the opening bell for a historic $81 billion initial public offering, a tightly orchestrated coalition of far-left, socialist, environmental, anti-Israel and Democratic grassroots groups executed a staged street action outside, complete with linked-arm sit-ins, pre-printed banners and rapid-fire social media drops timed to hijack the news cycle. "This IPO has got to go! Hey, hey, ho, ho," the staged protesters chanted to a small cadre of photographers as the audience. "Shame! Shame!" a protester yelled to a few responding "Shame!" in response. A close look at Thursday’s demonstration reveals the coordinated protest infrastructure that lawmakers have long warned is engineered to "sow discord" rather than produce meaningful policy solutions. According to Fox News Digital's analysis, the protest was no organic, grassroots effort. Rather, 14 groups, several of them part of well-funded organizations with estimated combined annual revenues of $43 million, coordinated the protest with a careful run-of-show and media choreography. A Fox News Digital tracker of the Anthropic protest organizers reveals a well-orchestrated effort across multiple organizations. They represent a spectrum of views from socialists to far-left environmental groups and anti-Israel activists. items.summary_original: A California federal prosecutor embroiled in a legal battle over his own authority is heading to Florida to investigate the FBI’s 2022 raid on President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago estate. Two sources familiar with the investigation confirmed to Fox News Digital that First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli will serve as a special assistant tasked with investigating whether Biden Justice Department officials broke federal law when executing their search warrant on Mar-a-Lago. Essayli will continue to hold his position as first assistant U.S. attorney, splitting his time between Florida and Los Angeles, a source familiar said. Essayli’s inquiry into the Mar-a-Lago search, which initiated former special counsel Jack Smith’s classified documents case, is a part of a broader Justice Department probe. Attorney General Pam Bondi initially launched the "grand conspiracy" investigation in August 2025 to target Obama-era officials, but its scope has since expanded to examine allegations that Biden officials also conspired to unlawfully prosecute Trump. Essayli is the latest prosecutor tapped to oversee the investigation after the resignations of two other attorneys in the past few months. Just a few weeks ago, Jason Reding Quiñones, the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Florida, resigned abruptly. Fischer and Luján formed a bipartisan and bicameral working group for USF reform last year with Reps. Doris Matsui, D-Calif., and Richard Hudson, R-N.C. to find fixes for the program, which was first launched in 1996. The draft legislation, which was reviewed by Fox News Digital, would also increase the current USF tax on cell phone lines and impose no cap on USF spending — meaning there’s wiggle room to raise the tax down the line. Susan Collins, R-Maine, Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska, and Rand Paul, R-Ky., were not enough to pass a non-binding resolution that originally passed the House, pushed by Rep. Seth Moulton, D-Mass., in September. Like the previous war powers resolutions, this effort would have required the removal of troops engaged in hostilities not authorized by Congress in the region. Even if it had passed, it was a more symbolic move given that it was non-binding and would not have been sent to Trump’s desk. DEMOCRATS COULD ENTER CONGRESSIONAL MAJORITY IN A GOVERNMENT SHUTDOWN But in the background, Senate Democrats are eyeing another battleground to be more forceful with their desire to rein in the war: government funding. The deadline to either fully fund or extend current funding is Dec. 11. Senate Republicans have warned that their counterparts intend to use the process as a cudgel to stymie tax dollars meant for the war and are willing to shut down the government to do so. They discovered he was the judge assigned to hear their complaint, their U.S.-based cousin told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview. Masoud Nourmohammadi, the cousin of Taraneh and Romina Rahimi, alleged that the official had been involved in their interrogation and subsequently presided over the complaint they filed against the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). "As soon as they walk in, they see the exact person who tortured them and sexually assaulted them is the judge," Nourmohammadi said. IRAN'S REGIME CAME FOR TEENAGE TWINS; THEIR FATE OFFERS A GLIMPSE OF TEHRAN'S WIDENING DEATH CAMPAIGN He claimed the complaint was immediately dismissed by that same official. "The judge was their prosecutor during the building (of) the case, and he was the one that did the sexual assault on the kids and tortured them as a prosecutor and for the lawsuit he was assigned as a judge for that lawsuit," Nourmohammadi said. items.summary_original: A former Southern Poverty Law Center official who led its hate-group tracking work told FBI agents he tried to make the watchdog’s controversial "Hate Map" more ideologically balanced, while saying Christians and conservatives were the first staffers pushed out in what he called a "long-term coup" at the organization after he left in 2013. The former director said he pushed for a more evenhanded SPLC, arguing that its "Hate Map" — which lists conservative groups alongside Ku Klux Klan chapters — should also include left-wing extremists, including violent animal-rights and extremist environmental groups. However, the former director said the effort met resistance and that, as liberal leaders reshaped the organization, most of his 17-person team was replaced. "There was some kind of coup, long-term coup going on there between some, what I would — what I heard were some pretty liberal people, extreme people that had other ideas about what we were doing," the unnamed former director told agents, as first reported by The Daily Signal's Tyler O'Neil , who has been covering the SPLC's legal troubles. The warning was issued as Ukraine's president said he arrived in Berlin, Germany for talks with more than 40 partners aimed at ending the war, including with President Donald Trump's son-in-law and advisor Jared Kushner and U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff. "We will, of course, restore the bridge. The road section suffered serious damage," Putin reportedly added. items.summary: الکساندریا اوکاسیو-کورتز، نماینده ایالت نیویورک، با افزایش گمانه زنی ها در مورد آینده سیاسی او، درها را برای نامزدی احتمالی ریاست جمهوری 2028 باز می گذارد. اوکاسیو کورتز در پاسخ به این سوال که آیا در حال بررسی نامزدی ریاست جمهوری در سال 2028 است، گفت: "من فکر می کنم، در حال حاضر، این انتخابات اتفاق افتاده است. ما باید برای به دست آوردن نتایج برای مردم کار کنیم." سازمان مترقی کمپین راه اندازی می کند و از AOC می خواهد برای ریاست جمهوری نامزد شود، در حالی که پیشروها به کاندیدای سوسیالیست چشم، اوکاسیو کورتز، که از سوسیالیست های دموکرات آمریکا (DSA) شعبه نیویورک سیتی برای یک پوت حمایت شده است.
items.summary_original: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., is leaving the door open to a potential 2028 presidential bid as speculation grows over her political future. "I think, right now, this election just happened. We got to work on getting results for people," Ocasio-Cortez told Fox News Digital when asked whether she was considering a presidential run in 2028. The self-described democratic socialist also expressed a willingness to work with President Donald Trump on key legislative priorities as Democrats prepare to take control of the House following the 2026 midterm elections. PROGRESSIVE ORG LAUNCHES CAMPAIGN URGING AOC TO RUN FOR PRESIDENT WHILE PROGRESSIVES EYE SOCIALIST CANDIDATE Ocasio-Cortez, who has drawn support from the Democratic Socialists of America's (DSA) New York City chapter for a potential White House bid, emphasized her desire to advance legislation in the 120th Congress rather than focus on presidential politics. Asked whether Democrats should work with Trump instead of prioritizing impeachment proceedings and congressional investigations , Ocasio-Cortez expressed optimism about finding common ground. "I hope so," she told Fox News Digital. "You know, I hope that President Trump can sign a congressional stock trading ban into law," Ocasio-Cortez continued. The congresswoman also identified healthcare reform as a potential area for bipartisan cooperation, urging Trump to address changes to Medicaid that she warned could threaten coverage for millions of Americans. Farmers say the attacks have resulted in significant livestock losses and warn that poisoned food and water sources could also endanger other animals and nearby residents. An Israeli source told Fox News Digital that military officials are taking reports of animal poisoning on Jewish-owned farms in the West Bank, known more commonly in Israel as Judea and Samaria, describing the incidents as "agricultural terror." The trend gained attention following an investigation by The Press Service of Israel (TPS-IL) that identified a cluster of poisoning incidents at farms across the Binyamin region over the past 12 months. CHRISTIAN ZIONISTS TAKE ON ANTI-ISRAEL ‘PROPAGANDA’ FROM BIBLICAL HEARTLAND In a TPS-IL video, an Israeli farmer alleged that poisonings took place with substances placed within food such as dates and pita bread. items.summary_original: Thousands of people in Haiti took to the streets Tuesday in a show of support for Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele deploying troops to the country to combat violent armed gangs. The demonstration unfolded as Haiti's Minister of Justice and Public Security, Patrick Pélissier, prepared to travel to San Salvador to discuss anti-gang strategies and ongoing troop cooperation. The president reflected on the moment in a post on X, sharing a video capturing a sea of people chanting, dancing and cheering in celebration. "I never expected anything like this. I hear you loud and clear. I love you too. We will triumph. God will give us victory," Bukele said. BUKELE WARNS HAITIAN GANG LEADERS THAT HIS FORCES WILL 'FINISH' THEM AS HE DID IN EL SALVADOR According to Reuters, some demonstrators carried signs reading "Long live Bukele" and "Down with the gangs," while others voiced their support for the Salvadoran leader. "Only a week of operation, we can see the path to change in Haiti. We say thank you to Bukele for all the help he gives us," demonstrator Claudy Mayas said. Another demonstrator said Bukele was providing Haitians with the one thing they had been waiting years for. "Four years ago, I could not go to Champs de Mars. I couldn't go to the south of Haiti," a demonstrator, also identified as Claude, said. "We don’t ask much of the government. We don’t ask for jobs. We need only security." items.summary_original: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) warned Wednesday that Bahrain's monarchy faces an existential threat as Iranian drones and missiles targeted U.S. military installations in the Gulf kingdom. Tehran's warning came amid renewed attacks on Bahrain, home to the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet, and a regional expert warned of Iran's decades-long efforts to destabilize the island nation and assert territorial claims. "This is a regime that has tried to inflame tensions there for quite literally several decades and has claims to the island nation as well," Behnam Ben Taleblu , a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), told Fox News Digital. BAHRAIN INTERCEPTS IRANIAN DRONES TARGETING US RADAR AFTER 2-MONTH LULL IN GULF STRIKES "The Islamic Republic is also trying to use military force to evict the United States from the region," he added. In a warning directed at Bahrain's ruling Al Khalifa family, IRGC Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi accused the monarchy of cooperating with military action against Iran , relying on U.S. protection and challenging Shiite religious authority. "Colluding in the aggression against Islamic Iran, living inside the American security bubble, and encroaching on the authority of the Shiite religious leadership are three fundamental mistakes being made by the Al Khalifa regime," Mohebbi wrote on X . items.summary_original: People practicing the Islamic faith are poised to outnumber Christians globally by 2035, becoming the world's largest religion, according to a new study released by the Pew Research Center. The detailed report attributes the shift primarily to higher fertility rates and younger populations among Muslims, who are growing at a faster rate than other major faiths. "Around the world, we find that Muslims tend to have more children than non-Muslims, [and] they tend to be younger as a result of having more children in the past," Pew senior demographer Conrad Hackett told Fox News Digital. WHY PEOPLE REALLY STOPPED HAVING KIDS: NEW STUDY UNCOVERS THE SURPRISING REASONS FAMILIES ARE SHRINKING Muslims have the highest fertility rate at 3.1 children per woman, followed by Christians at 2.5, according to the study. Between 2020 and 2025, Muslim women gave birth to 252 million babies, more than women of any other religion and compared to 208 million born to Christian mothers. If trends continue, the United States will also undergo a major religious shift . While Christians currently account for roughly 62% to 64% of U. Federal prosecutors announced the indictment Tuesday, seven months after Daithi O'Corrain, 48, allegedly breached the security perimeter at Shannon Airport in western Ireland and broke into an unoccupied U.S. Air National Guard C-130H Hercules aircraft. Prosecutors said O'Corrain then spent hours damaging the aircraft, cutting critical wiring and hydraulic lines, smashing cockpit instruments, puncturing air ducts and pinching shut the aircraft's liquid oxygen line. 2 FOREIGN NATIONALS BREACH UK BASE HOUSING KEY US, NATO INTEL HUB AMID $556M EXPANSION The damage was so extensive it rendered the aircraft inoperable, and the $60 million plane will never return to active flight status, according to federal authorities. Photographs released by federal prosecutors show extensive damage inside the aircraft, including smashed cockpit instruments, severed wiring and damaged equipment. Other images show tools allegedly used in the attack and O'Corrain standing on the aircraft's roof before his arrest. items.summary_original: The U.S. Army is racing to hire contractors to build 17 reinforced concrete bunkers in Israel, Saudi Arabia and Lebanon to protect American and coalition troops from deadly missile and drone attacks, according to a government procurement notice posted Friday. The move comes amid escalating violence in the Middle East , where Iranian attacks on U.S. military installations have killed at least 23 American service members since war broke out in late February. On Tuesday, Iran also claimed responsibility for another strike on a U.S. military base in Bahrain, its third attack there in five days. BAHRAIN INTERCEPTS IRANIAN DRONES TARGETING US RADAR AFTER 2-MONTH LULL IN GULF STRIKES Kuwaiti air defenses also intercepted incoming drones as Israeli forces launched new strikes in eastern and southern Lebanon. The Army plans to build 10 bunkers in Israel, five in Saudi Arabia and two in Lebanon, replacing makeshift shelters made from shipping containers. "Due to elevated regional force protection conditions, there is an urgent, high-priority requirement to replace nonstandard personnel protection shelters (e.g., converted shipping containers) and provide standardized, precast, reinforced concrete Indirect Fire bunkers," the Army said in the notice. "The objective is to safeguard U.S. and coalition service members operating in potentially hostile environments across multiple countries in [U.S. Central Command] Area of Responsibility," the notice added. items.summary_original: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is accelerating his nuclear program, expanding a uranium enrichment facility that can produce plutonium for nuclear weapons, the United Nations' nuclear watchdog warned Wednesday, calling Pyongyang's growing program a "cause for serious concern." International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Director General Rafael Grossi said the latest construction at the Yongbyon nuclear complex began in mid-September and was externally complete by late October, raising fresh alarms about North Korea's production of weapons-grade nuclear material. "The ongoing expansion of the DPRK's uranium enrichment programme remains a cause for serious concern," Grossi said in remarks to the IAEA's board of governors in Vienna , referring to North Korea by its official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. items.summary_original: Ukraine's military said it struck "one of the largest oil refineries in southern Russia" in the lead-up to President Donald Trump's meeting Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump will meet one-on-one with Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, China, a U.S. official confirmed to Fox News on Wednesday. The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine said explosions "rocked" Russia's Krasnodar Krai region last night and into this morning as Ukrainian forces "carried out air strikes against the Ilsky and Afipsky oil refineries, two key fuel suppliers in southern Russia." "Explosions and smoke were reported in the vicinity of the Ilsky Oil Refinery. Storage tanks were hit," it added. "The Ilsky Oil Refinery is one of the largest oil refineries in southern Russia, with an annual processing capacity of approximately 6.6 million tons of crude oil. Its products are used, among other purposes, to meet the fuel requirements of the aggressor state's armed forces." items.summary: صدها ایرانی با شعار مرگ بر دیکتاتور به خیابان ها ریختند. گزارش‌ها حاکی از آن است که در پی تصادف مرگبار اتوبوس در آخر هفته که منجر به کشته شدن 13 کارمند یک شرکت پالایشگاه نفت شد، و سایر پیام‌های ضد دولتی. نمایش نادر خشم ضد دولتی روز سه شنبه در آبدانان، شهری در غرب ایران در نزدیکی مرز این کشور با عراق آشکار شد. تظاهرکنندگان خواستار استعفای مقامات شرکتی شدند که عامل این حادثه هستند. به گزارش خبرگزاری میزان به نقل از رادیو اروپای آزاد، امرالله میسایی، دادستان محلی گفت: با کسانی که از این حادثه برای اخلال در نظم عمومی و تحریک عواطف مردم سوء استفاده کنند، قاطعانه برخورد خواهد شد. این رسانه به نقل از خبرگزاری فارس ایران همچنین گزارش داد که حدود 1000 نفر در این تظاهرات شرکت کردند.
items.summary_original: Hundreds of Iranians took to the streets chanting "Death to the dictator!" and other anti-government messages in the wake of a deadly bus crash over the weekend that killed 13 employees of an oil refinery company, reports said. The rare display of anti-government anger unfolded Tuesday in Abdanan, a city in western Iran near the country's border with Iraq. Demonstrators called for the resignation of company officials blamed for the accident. "Those who seek to exploit this incident to disrupt public order and inflame people’s emotions will be dealt with decisively," local prosecutor Amrollah Meysaei was quoted by Iran's Mizan news agency as saying, according to Radio Free Europe. The outlet, citing Iran's Fars news agency, also reported that an estimated 1,000 people took part in the protests, making them the largest demonstrations since mass unrest swept across Iran at the beginning of this year. Some of the protesters reportedly tried to damage public property. A video shared by HRANA, a rights group based outside Iran, also showed a crowd of protesters marching through the center of Abdanan, calling for accountability for the road accident. items.summary_original: Hundreds of protesters poured into the streets of western Iran on Tuesday following a deadly bus crash that killed 13 oil and gas workers, with demonstrations quickly escalating into anti-government chants with some protesters calling for the return of the Pahlavi monarchy. The unrest erupted in Abdanan, a city in Iran's Ilam province near the Iraqi border, where residents initially gathered to demand accountability for Saturday's fatal accident before turning their anger toward the Islamic Republic's leadership. Videos obtained by Fox News Digital showed large crowds marching through the streets, chanting "Death to the dictator!" IRANIAN PROTESTER HANGED HOURS AFTER MARRYING HIS IMPRISONED FIANCÉE OVER JAIL PHONE LINE Iranian-American journalist and foreign policy analyst Lisa Daftari said the demonstrations underscore the deeper political tensions facing Tehran. "Abdanan is a reminder that the Islamic Republic sits on top of a dormant volcano," Daftari told Fox News Digital. "These uprisings start with different catalysts, and in this case it was a local grievance, but they always arrive at the same conclusion." "The slogans we hear are ‘Death to the Dictator’ and ‘Javid Shah,’ not complaints about a policy. They are an indictment of the entire system, top to bottom," she said. items.summary_original: Eight decades after the Holocaust , Germany's conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that accepting the nation's responsibility for the Nazi genocide is an obligation that extends fully to immigrants arriving from Islamic countries. During an official reception for Germany’s Maccabiah Jewish sports delegation in Berlin on Nov. 6, Merz said the "historical responsibility of our country applies just as much to those who come here to Germany from Islamic countries, and anyone who fails to abide by this must leave our country." His response came after a basketball coach told him athletes feared being attacked if they wore their red Maccabi training jackets bearing the Star of David on German streets. The German Press Agency, dpa, reported that Merz quoted former German President Richard von Weizsäcker, who in 1985 told the Bundestag that "young people are not responsible" for the crimes of the Nazis, "but they are responsible for what becomes of it in history." Merz said the principle was "set in stone," and that, "given the current circumstances," von Weizsäcker’s words "also apply to immigrants who come to Germany," referring to recent antisemitic offenses committed by Muslim immigrants. items.summary_original: Iran's army targeted U.S. assets, including drone and missile sites, at Ali Al Salem base in Kuwait on Tuesday, according to Iranian state media. Kuwait's army appeared to corroborate the attacks, reporting that its air defense systems were combating a series of hostile drone strikes. "Kuwaiti air defenses are currently countering hostile drone attacks. The General Staff of the Army notes that any explosion sounds heard are the result of air defense systems intercepting hostile attacks. Everyone is requested to comply with the security and safety instructions issued by the relevant authorities," the army wrote in an X post. BLINKEN WARNS US GROUND INVASION OF IRAN WOULD BE 'ABSOLUTE DISASTER' AS TEHRAN ESCALATES ATTACKS The attacks are Iran's first on Kuwait in over two months. The Islamic Republic also reportedly targeted another U.S. ally in the Gulf on Wednesday, as Bahrain's General Command reported intercepting multiple Iranian aerial attacks . IRAN ESCALATES IN HORMUZ, CLAIMS STRIKE ON OMANI ISLAND IT SAYS 'ENEMY' USES FOR US MILITARY OPS Iran's attacks come shortly after the U.S. struck an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile site on Iran's Qeshm Island on Tuesday. That attack was a response to Iran targeting a U.S. radar installation at the Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain . items.summary: پاپ لئو چهاردهم روز دوشنبه پس از اصابت تسبیح پرتاب شده توسط یک نمازگزار در پرو، سکوت خود را شکست و در مورد این حادثه شوخی کرد و همچنین برای اولین بار جزئیاتی در مورد تشخیص سرطان و عمل جراحی بزرگ خود که قبل از سفر اخیرش به آمریکای جنوبی انجام شد، فاش کرد. پاپ که لوب پایینی ریه راستش را در 13 اکتبر برداشته بود، پس از اینکه پزشکان یک تومور سرطانی را پیدا کردند، در پرواز خانه به رم به خبرنگاران گفت که هنوز به طور کامل بهبود نیافته است، اما گفت که مصمم است این سفر 12 روزه را که مدت ها برنامه ریزی شده بود، تکمیل کند. لئو، 71 ساله، در طی یک کنفرانس خبری تقریبا 45 دقیقه ای در هواپیمای پاپ که از لیما، پرو باز می گشت، گفت: «همانطور که همه می دانند، فقط یک ماه پیش، من تحت عمل جراحی نسبتاً بزرگی قرار گرفتم. پاپ لئو در حالی که روزهای بعد از نماز فرشته را تحویل می دهد از بازگشت استقبال کرد
items.summary_original: Pope Leo XIV broke his silence Monday after being struck in the face by a rosary thrown by a worshipper in Peru, joking about the incident while also revealing details for the very first time about his cancer diagnosis and major surgery which took place before his recent trip to South America. The pope, who had the lower lobe of his right lung removed Oct. 13, after doctors found a cancerous tumor , told reporters on the flight home to Rome that he has not fully recovered, but said he was determined to complete the long-planned 12-day journey. "Just over a month ago, as everybody knows, I underwent rather major surgery," Leo, 71, said during a roughly 45-minute news conference on board the papal plane returning from Lima, Peru. POPE LEO WELCOMED BACK AS HE DELIVERS ANGELUS PRAYER DAYS AFTER LUNG CANCER SURGERY "But from the very beginning, I had in mind that this trip had been planned and that I was going to make it happen." The pontiff credited his recovery to prayer, medical care and personal determination. "So, with God's help — and I firmly believe in the power of prayer, as I have literally received messages from all over the world — together with a certain personal determination, which I also have, and with the help of the doctors, it proved to be possible." Despite the demanding itinerary that included multiple flights and appearances before massive crowds in Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, Leo acknowledged that he is still regaining his strength. items.summary_original: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un was photographed sitting in an ornate, throne-like armchair in the middle of a snowy ski resort while his daughter, viewed as his likely successor, carved down the slopes during an unusual family outing. The striking images, released Monday by North Korean state media, show Kim wearing sunglasses and dress shoes while seated in the elaborate upholstered chair, holding a lit cigarette. Other photographs show his daughter skiing in an all-white outfit as officials navigate the slopes nearby. The girl, believed to be named Kim Ju Ae, has increasingly appeared alongside her father at high-profile public events. South Korea's National Intelligence Service has assessed that she is being positioned as his likely successor, although North Korea has not publicly confirmed a succession plan. TRUMP ARRIVES IN PHILIPPINES AHEAD OF XI JINPING SUMMIT IN CHINA AFTER GOP MIDTERM LOSSES The snowy spectacle unfolded just as President Donald Trump raised the possibility that Kim could make an unexpected appearance during his upcoming high-stakes meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. "We might have Kim Jong Un. He may come, I don't know. That's up to President Xi," Trump told reporters Monday. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump was serious about potentially meeting Kim, though no talks were confirmed.
